recent_posts.title: 2025 Recap: so many projects
recent_posts.summary: A developer shares their 2025 journey building numerous interconnected Rust projects. Key projects include facet (a reflection-based serialization library with JIT compilation), dodeca (a static site generator with advanced caching), rapace (an IPC/RPC framework using shared memory), picante (an async query system inspired by salsa), and vixen (an ambitious build tool aiming to combine buck2's performance with cargo's ergonomics). The author also created supporting tools like arborium (tree-sitter grammar distribution), pikru (diagram rendering), and various format parsers. Most projects dogfood each other, forming an integrated ecosystem focused on developer experience, build performance, and comprehensive caching.

recent_posts.title: My gift to the rustdoc team
recent_posts.summary: Arborium is a new open-source project that brings tree-sitter-based syntax highlighting to Rust documentation. It bundles 96 language grammars into Rust crates that compile to both native and WebAssembly targets. The project offers three integration approaches: a JavaScript/WASM script for immediate use on docs.rs, a rustdoc PR to add native highlighting support, and a post-processor that adds highlighting to existing HTML documentation with minimal size overhead. The solution addresses long-standing limitations in docs.rs by providing accurate, comprehensive syntax highlighting without requiring full documentation rebuilds.

recent_posts.title: Evaluating Dioxus as a full stack Rust web framework
recent_posts.summary: An in-depth review of Dioxus, a Rust-based full-stack web framework that promises unified codebases across mobile, web, and desktop. The author explores Dioxus's server-side rendering, hydration process, and extensive hook system while comparing it to JavaScript frameworks like React and Svelte. Despite initial frustrations with debugging, hot-patching, and developer experience, the author acknowledges significant improvements in the main branch and recognizes the team's ambitious work on WASM tooling, though concludes the framework isn't quite ready to match JavaScript-based solutions in ergonomics.

recent_posts.title: Engineering a Rust optimization quiz
recent_posts.summary: A detailed account of building an interactive Rust optimization quiz for EuroRust 2025, covering the entire process from question design using Compiler Explorer to implementation with Dioxus framework. The author explores compiler optimizations like division-to-shift transformations, floating-point arithmetic edge cases, and memcpy recognition, while solving technical challenges including real-time voting, WebSocket reconnection handling, and scaling to hundreds of concurrent players. The project involved multiple playtesting sessions with Rust community members, last-minute features like GitHub OAuth and swipe gestures, and deployment on Kubernetes.

recent_posts.title: crates.io phishing attempt
recent_posts.summary: A phishing attack targeted crates.io maintainers through fake emails leading to fraudulent GitHub login pages. The crates.io team acknowledged the incident and is investigating. No compromised packages have been identified yet, but the attack follows a similar pattern to recent npm supply chain attacks.

recent_posts.title: color npm package compromised
recent_posts.summary: Josh Junon's npm account was compromised via a fake 2FA reset email, leading to backdoored versions of popular packages including 'color' (32M weekly downloads) and 'chalk'. The malicious payload appears designed to target crypto websites in browsers rather than server environments. The attack required multiple steps to be effective: upgrading dependencies, using them on the frontend, deploying to production, and users making transactions. Sindre Sorhus quickly republished chalk without the backdoor.

recent_posts.title: The science of loudness
recent_posts.summary: Explores the science behind different decibel measurements used in audio equipment, from sound pressure levels (SPL) measured by devices like Apple Watch to volume controls on amplifiers using dBFS. Covers the evolution of audio metering from 1930s BBC meters to modern LUFS standards that account for human hearing perception. Explains concepts like RMS, peak detection, loudness wars, and psychoacoustic filtering including A-weighting curves. Includes practical examples from YouTube's loudness normalization and workplace safety standards.

recent_posts.title: Summer fasterthanlime update
recent_posts.summary: Amos Wenger announces major changes to his fasterthanlime content platform, transitioning from 6-month exclusive articles to early access model with couple weeks exclusivity. Key updates include launching a Discord server with tiered channels, implementing dual RSS feeds (public and private), adding video early access, and discontinuing Ko-fi support in favor of Patreon and GitHub Sponsors. All previously exclusive content is now publicly available, and the creator plans more casual posting alongside polished long-form content.

recent_posts.title: All color is best-effort
recent_posts.summary: A video editing session reveals unexpected color rendering issues, specifically mysterious dots appearing in the final output. The author explores the layers of a composite image including a background stock photo with adjusted exposure settings, highlighting the complexities and unpredictable nature of color reproduction in digital media workflows.

recent_posts.title: Introducing facet: Reflection for Rust
recent_posts.summary: A new Rust library called 'facet' introduces reflection capabilities to the language. The author discusses their ongoing efforts to improve Rust compile times, including hardware upgrades to Apple Silicon and deep analysis of build performance. The post appears to be part of a premium content series exploring advanced Rust development techniques and optimization strategies.

Wenger expresses excitement for future enhancements, including efficient Docker image building, and encourages community contributions.
